text:
maria: Quick thread — we need agreement on how internal routing statuses map to client-facing HTTP codes and console badges. After the Canary incident customers saw a bunch of 502s wrapped by a fallback and got confused. Proposal: expose a stable, small set of client-facing statuses (200, 4xx, 429, 5xx) but add machine-readable headers + telemetry tags that explain the routing decision. Thoughts?

anil: +1 to headers. My worry: SDKs/PL customers often only parse HTTP code and message. If we rely only on headers, many won't surface the extra context. Can we add a short `client_hint` field in the JSON body (optional) for JSON APIs? e.g. `{"client_hint":"degraded"}`

suzanne: We should avoid changing response body shape mid-flight. Headers are safer. SDKs should map `X-RW-Route-Status` -> typed error object. Console can surface the richer reason. Also :eyes: on fraction of users who actually read headers — we need SDK support first.

lee: Implementation sketch: add headers `X-RW-Route-Status: degraded|healthy|failed` and `X-RW-Route-Reason: upstream|quota|rate_limit|config` plus `X-RW-Retry-Hint: none|immediate|backoff`. Telemetry tags: `route.status={healthy,degraded,failed}`, `route.reason={upstream,quota,cache}`. Map internal routing reasons to these canned values in the router. Example header block:```
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
X-RW-Route-Status: degraded
X-RW-Route-Reason: upstream
X-RW-Retry-Hint: backoff
```

anil: For retry semantics let's be explicit: `immediate` (safe to try once immediately), `backoff` (try with exponential backoff / jitter), `none` (do not retry). Also propose a `route_subcode` for telemetry only (e.g., `overflow`, `kv_cache_miss`, `placement_timeout`).

suzanne: Agree on `retry` vocabulary. Strong preference: `route_subcode` = telemetry-only for now. Don't expose subcodes to clients unless they are actionable. We should also define SLA thresholds that will trigger console alerts (example: `degraded_rate >= 5% over 5m` shows a banner).

maria: Clarifying policy questions: 1) If runtime falls back from a high-capacity variant to a cheaper model, do we return 200 with `X-RW-Route-Status: degraded` or 5xx? My take: return 200 for graceful fallback (best-effort) with `degraded` badge; reserve 5xx for failures where we couldn't serve meaningful output.

lee: +1 on that. Customers prefer a response rather than an error if the content is usable. This also keeps UI UX simple: badge + console timeline vs broken request. But we must mark those responses in telemetry as lower-quality and surface to customers (score, model_variant).

suzanne: SDK contract: we add Error.type = "degraded" when `X-RW-Route-Status=degraded` AND HTTP != 200. If HTTP==200 and degraded, SDK will return response but include `.meta.routeStatus = 'degraded'` and `.meta.retryHint` so app devs can decide. This keeps existing error flows intact.

anil: Docs note: publish migration guide + examples for handling headers and the SDK meta field. Link to spec draft: https://redwood.dev/routing-headers (WIP).

deploy-bot: deploy queued: add-routing-headers-to-runtime 2023-11-01T03:00Z :rocket:

lee: Two open questions: (A) exact naming (X-RW- vs X-Redwood-) — leaning `X-RW-` for brevity, (B) whether rate-limited responses get `degraded` or `failed` — I'd map `rate_limit` -> 429 with `route.status: failed` and `retry-hint: backoff` so clients get standard semantics.

maria: Good call. Summary / action items: 1) Anil to draft header names + canonical values and examples (PR to docs + SDK migration guide), 2) Lee to add telemetry tags and runtime mapping (PR to router), 3) Suzanne to update SDK error/meta contract + tests, 4) Maria to add Console card / alert for `degraded_rate`. We'll run a small canary for 2 weeks and monitor `degraded_rate` and `customer-impact` tags.

suzanne: ack
anil: on it
lee: starting PR now
maria: thanks everyone — tagging @eng-sre to monitor canary when deployed :thumbsup:
